A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SAT-HMR work and contain readable main text, equations, tables, figures and appendices. Retained, relocated and newly added material can be reliably matched.

before.justification: v1 reports original mesh-estimation experiments, benchmark comparisons and ablations in Tables 1–4 and supplementary Tables B1–B2.

after.justification: v3 retains the original empirical results and adds resolution, dataset-scale and scale-map experiments in the appendix.

M1.justification: The scale-adaptive encoder, background pooling, high-resolution token replacement, decoder, prediction heads and losses are retained. Ground-truth scale-map substitution is an added diagnostic control, not a change to the proposed inference method.

E1.justification: Training and evaluation retain the same datasets and mesh-estimation tasks, including AGORA, BEDLAM, 3DPW, MuPoTS and Panoptic. The new resolution settings and scale-stratified analyses operate within existing coverage. Figure B2's revised dataset attribution accompanies retained images.

E2.justification: The external SOTA comparator sets in Tables 1–3 remain unchanged. New Table B3 adds comparisons against the authors' single-resolution 644 baseline on the already-used 3DPW and Panoptic benchmarks; v1 reported this baseline on AGORA and BEDLAM but not those two benchmarks.

E3.justification: Additional experiments introduce mixed-resolution configurations, a threshold of 1.0, scale-map F1/MAE evaluation and ground-truth map substitution during inference. Section 4.2 also adds a ViT-L timing comparison. Existing benchmark splits and training settings remain unchanged. Table B3's Panoptic MVE label conflicts with Table 3's MPJPE reporting and does not establish an actual metric change.

E4.justification: v3 substantially broadens the diagnostic evidence with mixed-resolution sweeps, dataset scale distributions and per-scale baseline comparisons, and a predicted-versus-ground-truth scale-map control. The existing threshold study is extended with runtime measurements and the all-high-resolution setting. These additions test resolution allocation, dataset dependence and predictor accuracy beyond v1's retained ablations.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests. The new scale-map F1 and MAE values measure prediction accuracy rather than statistical uncertainty.

E6.justification: Main Tables 1–4 and matched original appendix rows retain their values, but substantial diagnostic results are added. Examples include BEDLAM MVE of 51.4 at resolution 896*, threshold-1.0 MVE of 57.9 at 46.4 ms, and scale-map F1/MAE of 0.98/0.056 with oracle MVE of 55.8 versus 56.0. These are added conditions and controls, not same-setting improvements over v1.

T1.justification: The scale definition, SMPL and joint representations, token construction, loss formulation and camera equations are unchanged. No new formal assumptions, mathematical derivations or proofs are introduced.

C1.justification: Both versions claim that scale-adaptive tokens preserve high-resolution accuracy while enabling real-time multi-person mesh estimation, including the same 24 FPS and up-to-fivefold speed claims. Naming SAT-HMR explicitly and adding examples of small-scale people do not redefine the contribution.

C2.justification: v3 adds a truncation-based hypothesis for larger people's dependence on background context, acknowledges absent gains for larger 3DPW instances, discusses instability at threshold 1.0, and interprets why predicted maps sometimes outperform ground-truth maps. Existing height/age-awareness and body-only limitations remain.

D1.justification: The implementation and reproducibility recipe in Section 4.2 and Appendix A is retained, including architecture depths, queries, optimizer, loss weights, camera assumptions, training budget, hardware and dataset sampling. New experimental configurations are covered under E3. The unchanged code/model link moves from the abstract to Figure 1's caption.

R1.justification: v3 adds eight references, including virtual-marker methods, ScoreHypo, Faster VoxelPose, PyMAF, MotionBERT and motion-related application literature. These expand citations around single-person estimation and applications without substantially changing the positioning of scale-adaptive encoding relative to earlier work.

P1.justification: Most existing prose and the section hierarchy are retained. Changes include expanded affiliations, corresponding-author information, acknowledgments, small wording clarifications and additional paragraphs in Appendix B. The new scientific material does not entail extensive rewriting of the existing narrative.

P2.justification: The appendix gains substantive resolution, dataset-comparison and scale-map tables B2, B3 and B5. The old threshold table becomes B4 with a runtime column and an additional row; the original speed–accuracy table moves from B1 to A1. Existing figures are retained, with limited caption and view-label corrections.

improvement.justification: The new controls and scale-specific breakdowns strengthen support for the existing method and clarify dataset-dependent limitations, especially through the scale-map oracle test and expanded threshold analysis. v1 already established the central trade-off with resolution, background-token and threshold ablations, so the gain is a focused strengthening. A new ambiguity tempers this benefit: Table B3 labels Panoptic errors as MVE although its 84.2 average matches Table 3's MPJPE.
